clue.text: Thoroughly impress Romeo from London area

indicators.note: from says the lover hails from that district, so the district word comes first

parts.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London
Romeo, Shakespeare's young hero, is the type of an ardent lover

explanation.surface: A Romeo hailing from a London district sweeps someone off their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW is a district of East London, famous as the home of the Bow Bells; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is an idiom for astonishing or overwhelming them completely.

clue.text: Mysterious commander coming before religious sect

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding in the British army
a cult is a small devoted religious group

explanation.surface: A shadowy military chief arrives ahead of a strange religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming before' just puts the commander first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult describes hidden, secret or supernatural matters, beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Being supple put a match to high explosive

parts.note: to put a match to something is to set it alight, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone flexible sets fire to a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'being supple' as a description, so it stands in for the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe describes a body that bends easily and moves gracefully, which is what being supple means.

clue.text: Taking place of another clergyman with debts

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England
IOUs (I owe you) are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A churchman in debt is replaced by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed; 'with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vicarious is experienced or done in substitution, through another person rather than oneself.

clue.text: Tag on again

parts.note: looks like adding something once more, but read as attaching a new tag or label a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To relabel is to give an item a fresh tag or name, attaching one once more.

clue.text: Unrestrained six hit out

indicators.note: out reads as outside: the word for hit goes round the six

parts.note: to lash is to hit hard, as with a whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A batsman freely strikes a six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit out' looks like the phrase meaning to attack, but 'out' stands alone as the signal for outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish spending or praise is profuse and extravagant, without restraint.

clue.text: Girl with a virus

parts.note: lass is a Scottish and northern word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman has caught a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa is a West African haemorrhagic fever virus, named after a Nigerian town.

clue.text: Game score with one extra

explanation.surface: A game where the score gets an extra point.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game's name is French for twenty-one, and a score is twenty, so one extra gives twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game, also called pontoon, whose name means twenty-one, i.e. a score of twenty plus one.

clue.text: The lady split on furniture designer

parts.note: the lady is referred to as she
to split on someone is to inform on them, which is also to rat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman broke up on a piece of furniture design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' in the sense of betraying or informing, as in 'split on a friend'. Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an English cabinet-maker whose name labels a neoclassical furniture style.

clue.text: Sour expert has contract

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
a tic is an involuntary contraction of a muscle

explanation.surface: A bitter specialist has signed an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a legal noun, but it is the verb for a muscle tightening, as in a tic.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means relating to vinegar, hence sharp-tasting and acid.

clue.text: Nerdy lass almost upset spartan general

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order
almost means the last letter of lass is dropped

explanation.surface: A geeky girl is nearly troubled by an austere military leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims lass to LAS; 'upset' then rearranges NERDY plus LAS. 'spartan' looks like 'austere' but names Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysander was the Spartan admiral who defeated Athens at Aegospotami in 405 BC.

clue.text: Sad nipper?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
a crab nips with its claws

explanation.surface: A gloomy small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like British slang for a small child, but it is a creature with pincers.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic crustacean with blue-tinged claws is literally a pincered creature coloured like gloom.

clue.text: American, one in new cult existing in reality

indicators.note: in places the one inside the rearranged word
new means the letters of cult are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: An American joins a fresh cult that really exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CULT into CTUL; 'in' puts A inside it to give CTUAL, after the A for American.
explanation.definitionFit: Actual means real, truly existing rather than imagined.

clue.text: Announcement from Roman Capitol

indicators.note: from means the answer is made out of these letters, reworked

explanation.surface: A decree issued from Rome's chief temple hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to make the answer from the letters of ROMAN CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclamation is a formal public declaration.

clue.text: Ineffective player being taken for a ride?

explanation.surface: A useless team member gets driven about.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'taken for a ride', usually meaning cheated, here meaning simply carried in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A team member who contributes nothing is carried by the others, and someone riding in a vehicle as traveller rather than driver.

clue.text: Mother pictured on computer

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to be pictured is to be in the frame of a photo

explanation.surface: Mum appears in a photo on a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large central computer serving many users is called by this term.

clue.text: Barred network on American-football field

explanation.surface: A grid of bars spread over a football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a grating of iron bars, as for grilling; the second is the field, marked with lines like a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating of parallel bars used for cooking, and US slang for the pitch in American football with its marked lines.

clue.text: Put out with part considered as representative

parts.note: put out means annoyed, which is cross
a section is a part of something

explanation.surface: Annoyed with the portion picked as typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like an action, but it is an adjective meaning irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample drawn so as to be typical of a whole population is a representative sample.

clue.text: Small crown made from empty ice-cream container

indicators.note: container means the ice-cream word holds the empty letter inside it

parts.note: in Britain a cornet is an ice-cream cone
O, a zero or nought, stands for empty

explanation.surface: A tiny crown fashioned from an empty ice-cream cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' signals that O goes inside CORNET, the British name for an ice-cream cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles below the rank of monarch.

clue.text: Director general gripped by strange urge, feeling of ill-will

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the rearranged word
strange means the letters of urge are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A boss in the grip of a weird impulse bears resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' gives GRUE, and 'gripped by' sets the director general inside it, after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is persistent resentment held against someone.

clue.text: Coming of Christianity

parts.note: read as the arrival of Christianity itself, but meaning an arrival, and the church season before Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival, and is the Christian season of preparation before Christmas.

clue.text: Inferior potato as you might say

indicators.note: as you might say means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: tattie is a Scots word for a potato

explanation.surface: A poor-quality spud, as people put it.
explanation.walkthrough: TATTIE is the Scottish word for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, of poor quality.

clue.text: In the matter of smartness at the plant

parts.note: re means concerning, in the matter of
finery is smart, showy clothing

explanation.surface: A remark about how well-dressed people are at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' means a factory, not something green.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial installation where oil or sugar is purified.

clue.text: Silently indicate agreement about mother becoming wanderer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the agreement word surrounds mother

parts.note: a nod shows agreement without words
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A wordless yes about mum turning into a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the nod round mother; 'becoming' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad has no fixed home and moves from place to place.

clue.text: Without 25 bothering organisation in south coast resort

indicators.note: organisation means the remaining letters are arranged in a new order
Without means that letter is taken away from the word bothering

parts.note: 25 points to the answer at 25 across, whose standard physics symbol is E

explanation.surface: Without any get-up-and-go, an organisation is troubled in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes E from BOTHERING, leaving BOTHRING; 'organisation' rearranges those letters. Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside town in East Sussex on the English Channel.

clue.text: A drama unfolding for the fleet

indicators.note: unfolding means the letters open out into a new order

explanation.surface: A play about a navy plays out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' rearranges the letters of A DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Armada is the name given to the Spanish fleet sent against England in 1588, and to any great fleet.

clue.text: Some keener gymnasts go

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few eager athletes have a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for vigour, as in 'full of go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Go, as in 'full of go', is a noun for vitality and drive.

clue.text: Right to finish in the row being more with it

indicators.note: in places right and finish inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A row on the right finish line is more fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets right and finish inside the row; 'with it' is an idiom for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendier means more fashionable, and 'with it' is an idiom for being up to date.
